children: An HMAC-signed POST fired to subscribers on every publish event — the push half of Barkpark's contract with downstream readers.

. When a Mutation commits a publish operation, Barkpark POSTs to each subscribed URL with the document payload. For a flat or default-scope mutation to fire, the webhook row must carry the default Workspace and Project — without that scope, the flat write (which Auth and Tokens authorizes on write alone) matches no subscriber and nothing is sent.
Each delivery is HMAC-signed. The signature rides a
: v1=<hex> for the digest plus a separate timestamp. Receivers recompute the HMAC over the body, compare against v1, and reject anything outside a
window — that bounds replay. A stable

retries, so an at-least-once delivery becomes effectively-once at the consumer. Delivery itself runs off the write path as an Oban Worker job, whose retry-with-backoff is what produces those retries when a subscriber is briefly down.

The headline subscriber is the Web Demo's receiver, which turns a publish event into Cache Revalidation — calling revalidateTag to bust the reader cache in ~1–2s instead of waiting on slow ISR. Publish events from Bulldocs paper ingest and ordinary Document edits both flow through this path. Webhooks are the realtime counterpart to the pull-based HTTP API v1 read routes.
